subject: ACME launch — traffic signal & temporary entitlement ramp approval
messages:
From: Isabel Garcia <isabel.garcia@acmecommerce.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: launch@acmecommerce.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME prod launch – traffic profiles and temporary quota request

Hi Ben / Marissa,

Thanks again for the run-through yesterday. Our launch is set for 2027-04-01 and the product team just finalized the traffic profiles. Quick ask: we need a temporary entitlement bump for the first 72 hours of launch to handle peak checkout personalization calls. Peak estimate attached (~1.1M requests in hour 2, sustained ~150k req/hour over first day).

What we need from Redwood:
- A temporary rate increase to ~6x baseline ingress for 72 hours starting 04/01 08:00 PDT.
- A fallback routing plan if quota is saturated (graceful degradation to cached responses or a cheaper model).
- A short checklist of infra/product steps we should take during the warmup window (KV cache priming, tokenization pre-warm).

We can sign a short-term commitment for the window if it helps. Attaching the traffic CSV and the launch playbook excerpt.

Attachments: acme_launch_estimated_traffic_v2.csv (csv), ACME_launch_playbook_excerpt.pdf (pdf)

-Isabel
Launch PM, ACME Commerce
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Isabel Garcia <isabel.garcia@acmecommerce.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME prod launch – traffic profiles and temporary quota request

Thanks Isabel — looping in infra and product. Quick internal summary of ask: temporary 6x ingress for 72 hours starting 2027-04-01 08:00 PDT + safe fallback to quantized model variant + cache-first routing.

Marissa / Kim / David, can you confirm the following by EOD tomorrow so we can get legal/ops alignment?
1) Feasibility: can Dedicated pools (or hosted soft-capacity) cover a 6x bump without violating other customers' SLOs? If not, what's the max sustainable uplift?
2) Fallback plan: recommended model variant for fallback (e.g., redwood-base-quant-q4) and expected latency/cost delta.
3) Product asks: KV cache priming endpoint, TTL recommendations, and any SDK guidance we should give ACME for warmup.
4) Monitoring: which metrics and dashboards (per-route qps, 95th/99th p99 latency, token burn rate, cache hit ratio) will we hand to ACME and when.

I drafted a short entitlement request PDF (attached) for legal/ops to sign; if we need a signed short-term commitment to open capacity that’s fine. Also, if product roadmap has any constraints (rolling changes, canary windows) that would block the exact 72-hr window, call that out here.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
Mobile: +1-415-555-0199
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Isabel Garcia <isabel.garcia@acmecommerce.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME prod launch – traffic profiles and temporary quota request

High level take from infra/product side: we can support an elevated ingress but need to split the ask across two levers to avoid SLA risk for others:
- Short-term uplift on hosted capacity pool (soft-burst) up to 4x baseline safely, with automated routing to dedicated reserved capacity if load exceeds threshold.
- Temporary canary lanes: route 20% of traffic to the full model and 80% to a cost-optimized quantized variant for the first 24 hours, then shift cadence based on errors/latency.

Technical asks for ACME (we should send these as a bullet list to them):
- Pre-warm plan: run a KV cache priming job 24h before go-live, push top-50 prefix keys (we'll provide an endpoint + simple script).
- Concurrency pattern: batch size guidance (we recommend continuous batching with max inflight 32 per worker for personalization endpoints).
- Retry/backoff config: client-side 429 backoff to 5s linear, then exponential after 3 retries.

Monitoring & rollbacks:
- We'll provide a temporary dashboard: per-route qps, 95/99 latency, error rate, model-fallback ratio, cache-hit %. Ops will page on sustained 5% error rate or p99 > 1.2s.
- If load > hard-threshold (we set at 1.5x hosted soft-burst), automatic fallback to dedicated reserved pool and then circuit-break to cached responses.

Attachments: redwood-entitlement-request-draft.pdf

Kimberly Park
Director, Platform Operations
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Isabel Garcia <isabel.garcia@acmecommerce.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME prod launch – traffic signal & temporary entitlement ramp approval

Isabel — thank you, and appreciate the quick turnaround on numbers. Summary & immediate asks below to get legal/ops and ACME aligned:

Summary decisions (accepted):
- Redwood to enable a temporary soft-burst uplift on hosted pool up to 4x baseline starting 2027-04-01 08:00 PDT for 72 hours.
- Canary routing: day 0–1 -> 80% quantized fallback / 20% full model; day 2 -> 50/50; day 3 -> revert to configured steady-state (subject to monitoring).
- Automatic escalation to ACME-dedicated pool if hosted soft-burst load exceeds 1.5x soft-burst threshold.

Immediate asks (action owners):
- ACME: run KV cache priming job 24h prior (Isabel) — we will share the priming script by EOD 3/18.
- Infra (Kim): confirm DNS / routing playbook and provide the temporary dashboard link + pager contacts by 3/18 COB.
- Product (Marissa): confirm there are no planned model changes in the 03/30–04/03 window that would change compatibility with the quantized fallback.
- Legal/Ops: we'll route the attached entitlement draft; Ben to coordinate signature if ACME signs.

Monitoring thresholds and rollback triggers are in-line with Kim's note — Ops will execute circuit-break to cached responses if p99 > 1.2s for 10 minutes or sustained error rate >5% for 5 minutes.

Isabel — if that summary looks good we will: 1) send the entitlement doc for short-term signature, 2) share the priming script and dashboard links, and 3) run a dry-run traffic injection on 03/25 to validate the routing and monitoring.

Thanks all — Ben
